editorial:
Ever wonder how your life would be different if you just missed your bus or hit a red light? That is exactly what happens to Helen, a stressed-out ad exec in London. After a bad day at work, she races for a train, and the story splits in two. In one version, she makes it. In the other, she misses it by a second. You get to watch both versions of her life play out at the same time. It is a cool, breezy ride that makes you think about fate and how the smallest choices can lead to totally different people and places.

The acting is great, especially since you get to see the lead actress play two different versions of the same person. The pacing is snappy and keeps you guessing which path will lead to a happier ending. While some of the romantic bits feel a little old-fashioned, the overall concept is still super fun. If you are in the mood for something light but thoughtful, you should definitely check it out.
endingExplained: In the end, both versions of Helen find a way to happiness. The version who missed the train finds a new love and a better life, while the version who caught the train eventually leaves her toxic boyfriend. The movie wraps up by showing that no matter which path she took, she was always meant to grow and find herself. It ends on a hopeful note, proving that fate helps you where you need to be.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic stories about fate and second chances.
